correctness.rationale: For \(n>5\), write \(\sigma(n)=kn+5\). Two distinct primes force \(k\ge2\) because \(1+p+q>5\). A strict divisor-ratio bound eliminates odd two-prime support. For \(n=2^a p^b\), parity forces even \(b\), and the exact equation \((2^{a+1}-p)(1+\cdots+p^{b-1})=6\) has no admissible solution. For odd three-prime support, \(k=2\) and parity makes \(n\) an odd square; the rational bound leaves \((p,q,r)=(3,5,7),(3,5,11),(3,5,13)\); reductions modulo \(5\) or \(3\) eliminate all three, independently of exponents. Even solutions have square odd parts by parity of odd-prime geometric sums. The full domain \(n>5\) and the small exception \(n=2\) for the pure congruence are explicit. The supplied `verify.py` was executed from its actual path and passed; finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The source sequence explicitly singles out remainder 5 as a difficult unresolved value and had only computational lower bounds. A complete exclusion for all odd integers with at most three distinct prime factors, combined with a necessary square odd part and at least three prime supports for all even integers, rules out infinitely many natural candidate strata by a genuinely unbounded argument. The result uses a finite trio of sharp support cases and modular obstructions rather than a numerical table, and supplies testable necessary forms for future work without claiming global resolution.
